readback_body:
## Description

**P1 — post-closure residual secret exposure in Session process discovery.** The accepted [#2514](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/2514) SC-08 establishes Agent-side redaction of ordinary secret flags, assignments, URL userinfo and Bearer values before Agent→Server transport. Its accepted [runtime record](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/41415322589) does **not** prove the separate argv case where a secret flag's value begins with a hyphen. Preserve that historical acceptance and track this independently; do not reopen #2514.

**Verified current-main static control flow (2026-11-08):** [redact.rs](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/crates/nession-agent/src/session/process_discovery/redact.rs) sets `expect_value = is_sensitive_flag(arg) && !arg.contains('=')`, but `sanitize_arg(arg, expect_value)` redacts the following argument **only if** `!arg.starts_with('-')`. The remaining argument passes through `split_assignment` / `redact_inline` without generic masking. Thus argv `["tool","--token","-secret123"]` yields display `tool --token -secret123` with no redaction for that value. The Agent's [process discovery](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/crates/nession-agent/src/session/process_discovery/mod.rs) uses this sanitizer to populate the Session-scoped process snapshot; the [architecture contract](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/docs/architecture/agent-process-discovery.md) explicitly requires redaction before transport.

## Reproduction

Deterministic regression fixture: call `sanitize(&["tool", "--token", "-secret123"], 512, 32)` and assert the display currently contains `-secret123` and `redacted == false`. Use an isolated child process whose argv contains the same flag/value shape and inspect its Session process snapshot if integration proof is needed. **Static result confirmed; executable fixture / live Agent→Server→Web readback pending.** Whether a particular external CLI accepts a leading-hyphen secret value depends on its parser; the sanitizer must not assume that all processes use the same CLI parser.

## Impact

A user opens Agent → current Session → process details (or copies the command). A secret-bearing process argv can be exposed to the authenticated browser and Server, violating the Agent-boundary sanitization contract. The problem is **not** an authentication bypass; it is an incomplete redaction rule for a permitted reader. No production credential exposure is claimed.

## Root Cause

The sanitizer uses `starts_with('-')` to avoid swallowing a subsequent option, but argv contains no parser metadata that proves a leading-hyphen argument is an option rather than a secret value. The current rule favors display fidelity over protection after an explicitly sensitive flag.

## Fix Direction / Scope

Make the Agent-owned redaction fail closed for the value position following a sensitive flag, including leading-hyphen values. Preserve readability of ordinary non-sensitive flags and avoid unnecessarily masking unrelated later arguments; define and test behavior for a missing value, `--` terminator and consecutive options. Keep the existing command byte/argv bounds, `redacted`/ `truncated` semantics, and Agent→Server contract unchanged.

**Non-goals:** general-purpose secret detection, raw argv reveal, new Web UI/prototype, process discovery redesign or credential logging for test evidence.

## Location

- `crates/nession-agent/src/session/process_discovery/redact.rs` (`sanitize`, `sanitize_arg`, `is_sensitive_flag`)
- `crates/nession-agent/src/session/process_discovery/mod.rs` (snapshot projection)
- Historical #2514 SC-08 / current `docs/architecture/agent-process-discovery.md`

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 The Agent command sanitizer never emits the value following a recognized sensitive flag, even when that value begins with `-`; deterministic negative fixtures include `--token -secret123`, an ordinary non-secret flag, consecutive flags and an absent value, and verify display plus `redacted` status.
- [x] SC-02 A Session process snapshot constructed from a controlled process with the leading-hyphen secret argv pattern contains only sanitized command material before it is forwarded to the Server, with no raw value in the serialized process command field; ordinary process discovery remains usable.

### Scenario mapping and proof

SC-01 → **SCN-01** deterministic security/parser contract; focused Rust sanitizer tests in isolated CI at exact PR SHA, positive and negative fixtures. SC-02 → **SCN-03** Agent Session process runtime, using the existing isolated Agent/tmux process discovery Case with a synthetic non-production token, snapshot serialization assertion and teardown. No real credentials, privileged host access, or production deployment required. Earliest proof: PR head, `method: case`; if the runtime Case cannot be executed, keep Pending rather than treating source review as a Pass.

## Acceptance Plan

```yaml

  SC-01:
    when: pr
    method: case
  SC-02:
    when: pr
    method: case
```

## E2E Verification

### New
- none: source-aligned Rust sanitizer and process snapshot Cases own the regression; no new browser interaction.

### Regression
- agent-process-discovery

## Product alignment

The current-Session-only process inspector remains useful and progressively disclosed, but its command display must not disclose credentials while preserving the user's working context. No UI change or prototype is needed.
